RIVERDALE ONCOLOGY CENTRE

Date of Consultation: 14/03/2024

CONSULTATION RECORD - NEW PATIENT ASSESSMENT

Patient Name: MARTINEZ, Carlos [redacted]
MRN: [redacted]
Date of Birth: 22/07/1958
Consultant: Dr. [redacted]

PRESENTING SITUATION

Mr. Carlos MARTINEZ is a 65-year-old gentleman who presents to the oncology service following a complex treatment course for small bowel gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST). The patient was initially diagnosed in February 2019 with a primary small bowel GIST, identified during investigation of intermittent abdominal pain and gastrointestinal bleeding. Following multidisciplinary team discussion, the patient underwent surgical resection of the primary tumour in April 2019, with histopathology confirming a 7.2cm GIST arising from the jejunum with intermediate-risk features. Staging at diagnosis revealed T3N0 disease, with no evidence of metastatic spread at that time.

MOLECULAR AND PATHOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS

The tumour underwent comprehensive molecular profiling at the time of initial diagnosis. Genomic sequencing identified a KIT exon 11 L576P point mutation, which is a well-recognised activating mutation associated with sensitivity to tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy. PDGFRA was not tested at that time. Tumour mutational burden assessment demonstrated TMB-low status at 2.8 mutations per megabase, consistent with the typical molecular profile of gastrointestinal stromal tumours. The pathological grade was documented as intermediate-risk based on tumour size and mitotic count.

TREATMENT HISTORY - SYSTEMIC THERAPY

Following surgical resection, Mr. MARTINEZ commenced adjuvant imatinib mesylate therapy at a dose of 400mg daily in June 2019. The patient tolerated this treatment remarkably well initially, with only mild periorbital oedema and occasional nausea managed conservatively. He continued on adjuvant imatinib for a planned duration of three years. During this period, surveillance imaging demonstrated stable disease with no evidence of recurrence. However, in August 2022, a routine surveillance CT scan demonstrated evidence of disease recurrence, with a 3.4cm nodular lesion identified in the small bowel mesentery, consistent with local recurrence. Following multidisciplinary team review and confirmation of disease progression, the imatinib dose was escalated to 800mg daily in September 2022. Subsequent imaging in December 2022 demonstrated partial response to dose escalation, with reduction in the size of the recurrent lesion to 2.1cm.

In March 2023, the patient was discussed at the specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary meeting regarding potential enrollment into a clinical trial evaluating novel KIT inhibitors for imatinib-resistant GIST. After detailed discussion with Mr. MARTINEZ and his family, the patient was screened for the trial but unfortunately did not meet eligibility criteria due to the demonstrated response to imatinib dose escalation. He therefore continued on imatinib 800mg daily with ongoing surveillance.

TREATMENT HISTORY - RADIOTHERAPY

In May 2023, following identification of progressive disease in the mesenteric lesion despite dose-escalated imatinib, with the lesion measuring 3.8cm on CT imaging, the patient was referred for consideration of stereotactic body radiotherapy. Following detailed planning and multidisciplinary discussion, Mr. MARTINEZ underwent SBRT to the mesenteric recurrence, receiving 40 Gy in 5 fractions completed in June 2023. Post-radiotherapy imaging in September 2023 demonstrated excellent local response with significant reduction in the size of the treated lesion and resolution of metabolic activity on PET-CT scanning. This represented a clear positive treatment response. Concurrently, the patient experienced significant improvement in his abdominal discomfort, which had been progressively worsening prior to radiotherapy. This symptomatic improvement was maintained for several months following completion of radiotherapy.

TREATMENT HISTORY - SECOND SURGICAL INTERVENTION

Despite the excellent initial response to radiotherapy, surveillance imaging in January 2024 identified a new 2.3cm lesion in the ileal mesentery, separate from the previously treated site, consistent with further disease recurrence. Following comprehensive restaging, which confirmed no evidence of distant metastatic disease, the patient underwent further surgical exploration and resection of the recurrent mesenteric disease in February 2024. Intraoperatively, a discrete mesenteric nodule was identified and completely excised with clear margins. Histopathology confirmed recurrent GIST with similar morphological features to the primary tumour. The post-operative recovery was complicated by a small bowel ileus, which resolved with conservative management, and Mr. MARTINEZ was discharged on post-operative day 8.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Mr. MARTINEZ is a retired civil engineer who lives with his wife in [redacted]. He has excellent family support, with two adult children living locally who are actively involved in his care. He is a lifelong non-smoker and consumes alcohol only occasionally, approximately 2-3 units per week with meals. Prior to his recent surgery, he was independently mobile and managing all activities of daily living without assistance. He maintains an active social life and has continued to participate in his local community gardening group when his health permits.

CURRENT SYMPTOMS AND PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

At today's consultation, Mr. MARTINEZ reports that his post-operative abdominal pain has now completely resolved, which represents significant improvement from his presentation two months ago. He had previously reported moderate abdominal pain, rated 5-6/10, which was interfering with his daily activities. He does report ongoing fatigue, which he describes as moderate in severity, affecting his ability to complete his usual daily tasks. He mentions that he experiences occasional early satiety, particularly when consuming larger meals. His weight has remained stable over the past four weeks, following an earlier period where he lost approximately 4kg in the three months prior to his recent surgery.

On physical examination today, Mr. MARTINEZ appears generally well, though demonstrates some evidence of weight loss with mild temporal wasting. His vital signs are stable. Abdominal examination reveals a well-healed midline laparotomy scar with no evidence of herniation. The abdomen is soft and non-tender throughout, with normal bowel sounds present. There is no palpable organomegaly, and specifically no palpable masses or lymphadenopathy detected on careful examination. There is no clinical evidence of ascites. Examination of other systems is unremarkable.

CURRENT DISEASE STATUS AND RECENT INVESTIGATIONS

Most recent CT imaging from 10/03/2024 demonstrates post-surgical changes in keeping with recent mesenteric resection, with no evidence of residual disease at the site of recent surgery. Importantly, there is no evidence of new metastatic disease, with the liver, lungs, and peritoneum appearing clear of metastatic deposits. The radiological report specifically states no evidence of metastatic spread. Baseline post-operative blood investigations demonstrate haemoglobin 128 g/L, white cell count 6.8 x10^9/L, platelets 245 x10^9/L, and normal renal and hepatic function.

PERFORMANCE STATUS

Mr. MARTINEZ's current performance status is ECOG 1, reflecting his good overall functional status with some limitation in physically strenuous activity but ability to carry out light work and self-care activities independently.

MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM DISCUSSION AND FUTURE MANAGEMENT PLAN

This case was discussed at the specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary meeting held on 12/03/2024. Given the patient's complex treatment history with multiple lines of therapy including surgical resection, adjuvant and escalated-dose imatinib, stereotactic radiotherapy, and further surgical intervention, there was extensive discussion regarding optimal ongoing management. The consensus recommendation is to recommence systemic therapy with consideration of switching to an alternative tyrosine kinase inhibitor given the pattern of recurrence on imatinib.

The specific management plan agreed is as follows:

1. Recommencement of systemic therapy: Given the KIT exon 11 mutation status and the history of disease recurrence on standard-dose imatinib, there was discussion regarding reintroduction of dose-escalated imatinib versus switching to sunitinib. The MDT recommendation is to commence sunitinib 50mg daily on a 4-weeks-on, 2-weeks-off schedule as second-line therapy. This plan has been discussed in detail with Mr. MARTINEZ today, including potential adverse effects such as fatigue, hypertension, hand-foot syndrome, and myelosuppression.

2. Clinical trial re-evaluation: The MDT has recommended that Mr. MARTINEZ should be re-evaluated for potential clinical trial enrollment, specifically for trials investigating novel KIT inhibitors or combination strategies in advanced GIST. The research team will review current available trials and contact the patient if suitable options become available.

3. Surveillance imaging: Baseline CT chest, abdomen and pelvis to be performed 8 weeks following commencement of sunitinib to assess early treatment response. Subsequently, 3-monthly surveillance imaging will be maintained.

4. Supportive care: Referral to the dietetics service for nutritional optimization given recent weight loss and early satiety. Routine monitoring of blood pressure given planned sunitinib therapy. Continuation of proton pump inhibitor therapy. Anti-emetic medication prescribed as required.

5. Ongoing multidisciplinary review: Case to be discussed at the specialist sarcoma MDT following first restaging scan, with ongoing review of systemic therapy options including consideration of clinical trial enrollment if disease progression occurs.

Mr. MARTINEZ expressed understanding of the treatment plan and is agreeable to commencing sunitinib therapy. He will be reviewed in clinic in 2 weeks following commencement of treatment to assess tolerability, and routine follow-up will be maintained throughout treatment.

Dr. Patricia Hammond
Consultant Medical Oncologist
Riverdale Oncology Centre
